title: In vitro degradation and biocompatibility evaluation of typical biodegradable metals (Mg/Zn/Fe) for the application of tracheobronchial stenosis

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Tracheobronchial stenosis stents need a biodegradable metal with suitable degradation and airway-cell compatibility. Degradation and cytocompatibility of Mg, Zn and Fe have not been compared under airway-relevant in-vitro conditions.
states.detail: Absorbed: b1 (HYP/need), b2 (HYP/gap), b3 (DES/base_system), b4 (DES/variable_sweep), b5 (DES/method), b6 (PRC/stimulus), b16 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: HP-Mg surfaces are pitted in GS and deeply attacked in SBF; HP-Zn and P-Fe stay largely intact. SBF corrosion products on HP-Mg and HP-Zn are Ca-P-rich oxides; GS products carry little Ca and P

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Chloride-rich SBF breaks down surface films and speeds dissolution, most for Mg, while Ca-P precipitates onto products. Electrochemical corrosion tendency ranks Mg > Zn > Fe; SBF lowers Ecorr and raises icorr, most for Mg.
states.detail: Absorbed: b11 (MEC/pathway), b9 (PRP/value), b10 (PRP/value), b13 (MEC/pathway), b12 (PRP/value). Premises: Chloride ions destabilise Mg(OH)2 and passive films, accelerating dissolution of Mg and other active metals; More negative Ecorr and higher icorr indicate higher corrosion tendency and rate; CCK-8 absorbance at 450 nm scales with the number of viable cells

states.title: Performance state
states.head: HP-Zn best combines moderate degradation with airway-cell compatibility for a biodegradable tracheobronchial stent

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Mg degrades fastest, Fe slowest but suppresses A549 cells; Zn gives intermediate degradation with good cytocompatibility

nodes.title: MICRO, F2

nodes.solves: HP-Mg surfaces are pitted in GS and deeply attacked in SBF; HP-Zn and P-Fe stay largely intact
nodes.note: HP-Zn in SBF at 14 d shows dark flaky product patches; P-Fe surfaces stay featureless at 500 um scale

nodes.title: EDS:spectrum, F3

nodes.solves: SBF corrosion products on HP-Mg and HP-Zn are Ca-P-rich oxides; GS products carry little Ca and P
nodes.op: assign features, compare across conditions, cross check consistency
nodes.note: base-metal signal falls to ~6 at% (Mg) and ~3 at% (Zn) in SBF vs ~51 and ~20 at% in GS, i.e. thicker product layers in SBF EDS (F3a) gives only ~1 at% P for HP-Mg-GS against ~12 at% for HP-Mg-SBF

nodes.title: MICRO, F5
nodes.head: Fluorescence: P-Fe IC has scattered cells at 2 and 4 d, sparse EC cells at 4 d; Mg, Zn near-confluent
nodes.solves: HP-Mg and HP-Zn support A549 growth in IC and EC; P-Fe suppresses viability in IC and, by day 5, EC

nodes.solves: Electrochemical corrosion tendency ranks Mg > Zn > Fe; SBF lowers Ecorr and raises icorr, most for Mg
nodes.op: compare across conditions, fit model, read characteristic point
nodes.detail: o1: PDP Ecorr: Fe about -0.70/-0.77 V, Zn -1.21/-1.27 V, Mg -1.52/-1.77 V vs SCE in GS/SBF; o2: icorr: HP-Mg-SBF ~18 uA/cm2, HP-Zn-SBF ~5.6, all others below ~2 uA/cm2; o3: In GS, HP-Mg icorr (~1.4 uA/cm2) is not above HP-Zn (~1.7) or P-Fe (~1.1)

nodes.head: SBF corrosion rate: HP-Mg 3.4 mm/y at 7 d, ~2.0 by 21-28 d; Zn <=0.55, Fe <=0.27; GS all <=0.8
nodes.solves: Immersion degradation rate ranks Mg >> Zn > Fe and is far higher in SBF than in GS
nodes.detail: o7: SBF corrosion rate: HP-Mg 3.4 mm/y at 7 d, ~2.0 by 21-28 d; Zn <=0.55, Fe <=0.27; GS all <=0.8
